title: Distribution of One Benefit Payment Among Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders
content:
When a benefit payment carries more than one deduction under Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders, the payment is distributed among them as follows.

## Clauses

**1. Sequence.** Deductions are taken from each benefit payment after any overpayment offset, one order at a time in the order of the kinds' deduction priority (rank 1 first), each from the available net.

**2. Available net.** The available net for an order is the payment's gross payable amount, less the overpayment offset taken from that payment, less the deductions already taken from that same payment by orders of higher priority.

**3. Combined cap per kind.** Every kind's combined cap applies to all of the claimant's orders of that kind together. The cap is the kind's cap share multiplied by the payment's net payable after the overpayment offset (the gross payable amount less the overpayment offset).

**4. Several child support orders.** Several child support orders of one kind share their combined cap in proportion to their weekly amounts, each share rounded to the cent, with any rounding remainder going to the order received first.

**5. Payment short of the amount due.** A deduction that cannot be taken in full from the available net is taken in part where the kind allows partial deductions; otherwise, or when the available net is below the kind's minimum net, it is skipped and recorded as skipped for insufficient net.

**6. No make-up.** A skipped or partial deduction is never made up from a later payment.

**7. Income tax deductions.** Income tax deductions are computed on the gross payable amount, so their amount does not change with the overpayment offset, but they are still taken only from what remains after higher-priority deductions.

## Outcome for one order

| Available net compared with the kind's minimum net | Available net compared with the amount due | Kind allows partial deductions | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Below the minimum net | — | — | Skipped, insufficient net |
| Not below the minimum net | At least the amount due | — | Taken in full |
| Not below the minimum net | Less than the amount due | Yes | Taken in part: the whole available net |
| Not below the minimum net | Less than the amount due | No | Skipped, insufficient net |

The amount due is the order's deduction as computed for that order, limited by its kind's combined cap (or, for several child support orders of one kind, by the order's share of that cap).

## Worked distribution (hypothetical figures throughout)

*The three kinds below are labelled A, B and C and given invented terms purely to illustrate the clauses; they are not the terms of any actual kind.*

Hypothetical payment: gross payable $300.00; overpayment offset $100.00; net payable after offset $200.00.

- **Kind A** (rank first; three child support orders with weekly amounts of $60.00 each; cap share 50%; partial deductions allowed; no minimum net). The combined cap is 50% of $200.00, which is $100.00. Shared in proportion to equal weekly amounts, each share is one third of $100.00, rounded to the cent: $33.33. The three shares total $99.99; the $0.01 remainder goes to the order received first, whose share becomes $33.34. Each weekly amount of $60.00 exceeds its share, so the deductions are $33.34, $33.33 and $33.33, a total of $100.00. Available net afterwards: $200.00 less $100.00, which is $100.00.
- **Kind B** (next rank; income tax at an invented 10% of gross payable; cap share 100%; partial deductions allowed). The amount is 10% of $300.00, which is $30.00, regardless of the offset. The available net of $100.00 covers it, so $30.00 is taken. Available net afterwards: $70.00.
- **Kind C** (last rank; an invented 20% of net after offset; cap share 50%; no partial deductions; minimum net $25.00). The amount due is 20% of $200.00, which is $40.00, within its $100.00 cap. The available net of $70.00 is not below $25.00 and covers $40.00, so $40.00 is taken.

Net paid to the claimant in this illustration: $200.00 less $100.00, less $30.00, less $40.00, which is $30.00.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

| Situation for Kind C (amount due $40.00, minimum net $25.00, no partial deductions) | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Available net $24.99 | Skipped, insufficient net (below the minimum net) |
| Available net $25.00 | Skipped, insufficient net (not below the minimum net, but less than the amount due and partial deductions are not allowed) |
| Available net $40.00 | Taken in full, $40.00 |

| Situation for Kind B (amount due $30.00, partial deductions allowed, no minimum net) | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Available net $12.50 | Taken in part, $12.50 |
| Available net $30.00 | Taken in full, $30.00 |

In each skipped or partial case, the next payment is distributed on its own figures; nothing is added to make up the shortfall.
